sentences.zh: 如果，呃，我们交谈的人愿意的话，他们会被随机分配到我们实验中的四种条件之一，

sentences.en: experiment, which involved me digging into my backpack, pulling out an envelope that had one of two different monetary amounts inside.
sentences.zh: 这涉及到我把手伸进背包，掏出一个信封，里面装着两种不同金额的钱中的一种。

sentences.en: So half of the folks were given a $5 bill.
sentences.zh: 所以一半的人拿到了一张5美元的钞票。

sentences.en: The other half were given a $20 bill.
sentences.zh: 另一半人拿到了一张20美元的钞票。

sentences.en: And along with the bill that they received were, it was a small slip of paper with some spending instructions.
sentences.zh: 随他们收到的钞票一起的，是一张写有一些消费说明的小纸条。

sentences.en: And so critically, half of these folks were asked to spend the money by the end of the day on a small gift for themselves.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，这些人中的一半被要求在当天结束前把钱花在给自己买的小礼物上。

sentences.en: And the other half were asked to spend the money on a gift for someone else or a charitable donation.
sentences.zh: 而另一半则被要求把钱花在给别人的礼物或慈善捐款上。

sentences.en: And we let them go on their merry way.
sentences.zh: 然后我们让他们高高兴兴地走了。

sentences.en: They did whatever they wanted to do with this money.
sentences.zh: 他们用这笔钱做了他们想做的事。

sentences.en: Um, we asked them to spend it by five o'clock and then a research assistant called them at the end of the day to see how they were feeling.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们要求他们在五点之前花掉，然后在一天结束时由一名研究助理打电话给他们，了解他们的感觉。

sentences.en: Um, and importantly, this research assistant didn't know what they had been asked to do or how they had been asked to spend the money.
sentences.zh: 嗯，重要的是，这位研究助理并不知道他们被要求做什么，也不知道他们被要求如何花这笔钱。

sentences.en: And we asked them in this phone call to report how happy they were feeling.
sentences.zh: 我们在电话里询问他们报告自己当时的幸福感。

sentences.en: And, and what we found was that it didn't matter so much, how much money people had received to spend.
sentences.zh: 结果我们发现，人们收到多少钱来花并不是那么重要。

sentences.en: What really mattered for their happiness at the end of the day was who they spent the money on such that people who spent the money on others were significantly happier
sentences.zh: 对他们一天结束时的幸福感真正重要的是他们把钱花在了谁身上，把钱花在别人身上的

sentences.en: than those who spent on themselves.
sentences.zh: 人明显比把钱花在自己身上的人更快乐。

sentences.en: And this question about whether being generous and specifically, whether being generous with our financial resources, um, is something that has fascinated me now for over a decade.
sentences.zh: 关于慷慨是否——具体来说，用我们的财务资源慷慨解囊是否能带来快乐——这个问题已经让我着迷了十多年。

sentences.en: And I've really been trying to understand, you know, is this something that those of us living in North America who are fortunate enough to have extra disposable income
sentences.zh: 我一直试图去理解，你知道，这是否只是我们这些生活在北美、幸运地拥有额外可支配收入的人

sentences.en: might simply get to enjoy, or whether this is something that is, you know, much more consistent
sentences.zh: 能够享受的事情，还是说这更符合

sentences.en: to the human experience, whether it might be something we can see in most countries and cultures, um, across the age spectrum and across different lived experiences.
sentences.zh: 人类的共同体验，是否我们在大多数国家和文化中、在各个年龄段以及不同的生活经历中都能看到这种现象。

sentences.en: And so we've run a number of studies.
sentences.zh: 所以我们做了很多研究。

sentences.en: I've had the great pleasure of collaborating with people from all around the world.
sentences.zh: 我有幸与来自世界各地的人合作。

sentences.en: But the other study I wanted to tell you about is, um, with young kids, because I wondered, you know, at what age do we begin to find giving rewarding?
sentences.zh: 不过我想跟你聊的另一项研究是，嗯，关于幼儿的，因为我想知道，你知道，我们在什么年龄开始发现给予是有回报的？

sentences.en: Um, and so partnering with a developmental psychologist and another social psychologist, we ran these studies where, um, we, we got toddlers just under
sentences.zh: 嗯，因此，通过与一位发展心理学家和另一位社会心理学家合作，我们进行了这些研究，嗯，我们找来了年龄不到

sentences.en: the age of two to come into the lab with a parent.
sentences.zh: 两岁的幼儿和父母一起进实验室。

sentences.en: Um, and they were taken through a five phase, like very brief.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们经历了五个阶段，非常简短。

sentences.en: It was just a few minutes, but they saw kind of a small puppet show and they got to interact with the puppets.
sentences.zh: 虽然只有短短几分钟，但他们看了一个小型木偶戏，并且有机会与木偶互动。

sentences.en: And so in the first phase, they met a stuffed animal monkey who liked eat it.
sentences.zh: 所以在第一阶段，他们遇到了一个喜欢吃东西的毛绒玩具猴子。

sentences.en: They, they found out likes eating treats.
sentences.zh: 他们发现它喜欢吃零食。

sentences.en: Then this child themselves received a few treats.
sentences.zh: 然后这些孩子自己收到了一些零食。

sentences.en: Um, and they were told they were, they got to eat them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们被告知他们可以吃掉这些零食。

sentences.en: They were just edible crackers that kids really enjoy.
sentences.zh: 那只是孩子们非常喜欢吃的小饼干。

sentences.en: And then critically over the next minute or so, they got the chance to give one of their own treats to the puppet.
sentences.zh: 然后至关重要的是，在接下来的大约一分钟里，他们有机会把自己的零食分一块给木偶。

sentences.en: They got to watch as the experimenter gave a treat to the puppet.
sentences.zh: 他们看着实验员给木偶一块零食。

sentences.en: Um, or they got to give one of the experimenters treats to the puppets.
sentences.zh: 嗯，或者他们可以把实验员的零食分一块给木偶。

sentences.en: So they either got to engage in costly giving or not costly giving.
sentences.zh: 所以他们要么参与了有代价的给予，要么是没有代价的给予。

sentences.en: Um, and every time the puppet got a treat, they ate it in a very excitable way.
sentences.zh: 嗯，每当木偶得到零食时，它都会以一种非常兴奋的方式吃掉。

sentences.en: And we wanted to know how the kids felt when they got to give.
sentences.zh: 我们想知道孩子们在给予时感觉如何。

sentences.en: And so we've, we learned that you can't just ask two-year-olds how happy they are because they say they're happy all the time.
sentences.zh: 因此我们了解到，你不能直接问两岁的孩子他们有多快乐，因为他们总是说自己很快乐。

sentences.en: So instead of what we did was we set up a video camera over their shoulder and we captured their facial expressions.
sentences.zh: 所以我们采取的做法是，在他们肩膀上方架设一台摄像机，捕捉他们的面部表情。

sentences.en: Um, and later we coded these for the extent to which the kids were smiling.
sentences.zh: 嗯，随后我们对这些表情进行了编码，以分析孩子们微笑的程度。

sentences.en: And what we found, I think was really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的结果，我认为非常迷人。

sentences.en: So first and foremost, we found that kids would smiled more when they gave away treats to the puppet than when they received the treats themselves.
sentences.zh: 首先也是最重要的一点，我们发现把零食分给木偶的孩子，比自己吃零食时笑得更多。

sentences.en: But critically, what I thought was so interesting and exciting was that kids smiled more when they gave, when they gave away a treat that belonged to them than when they gave
sentences.zh: 但至关重要的是，我认为非常有趣且令人兴奋的是，当孩子们送出属于他们自己的零食时，

sentences.en: away an identical treat that didn't.
sentences.zh: 比他们送出不属于自己的、完全相同的零食时笑得更多。

sentences.en: And so what my colleagues and I kind of argued is that even under the age of two, we see some evidence for the fact that people might feel good when they give.
sentences.zh: 因此，我和同事们所认为的论点是，即使在两岁以下，我们也能看到一些证据，表明人们在给予时可能会感觉良好。

sentences.en: Um, and perhaps especially when it involves a sense of self-sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 嗯，特别是当它涉及某种自我牺牲感时，或许更是如此。

sentences.en: So what happens when people don't have enough resources for themselves?
sentences.zh: 那么，当人们连自己的资源都不够时会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: If you're struggling with poverty or other hardships, can being generous still make you feel happy?
sentences.zh: 如果你正在与贫困或其他困境作斗争，慷慨大方还能让你感到快乐吗？

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: I mean, so I kind of alluded to this in my last question.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我在上一个问题中已经暗示过这一点了。

sentences.en: So I've had the good fortune of working with collaborators from all around the world to try to test this question in places where people might have objectively very little to give.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常幸运能与来自世界各地的合作者一起工作，尝试在那些人们客观上几乎没有什么可给予的地方检验这个问题。

sentences.en: Um, and the short answer is we see that even in places where people, and among samples where people are having trouble meeting their own basic needs,
sentences.zh: 嗯，简短的回答是，我们发现即使在那些人们、以及那些连满足自身基本需求都有困难的群体中，

sentences.en: they also feel good when they give.
sentences.zh: 他们在付出时也会感觉良好。

sentences.en: And I think one kind of important feature of the work that sometimes gets lost is that people don't need to be giving a lot to feel good about giving.
sentences.zh: 我认为这项工作的一个重要特征有时会被忽视，那就是人们不需要付出很多就能对给予感到高兴。

sentences.en: So in many of our experiments, people are giving the equivalent of $2.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们的许多实验中，人们付出的相当于2美元。

sentences.en: Um, you know, they're buying a chocolate bar for a sick kid at a local children's hospital or buying a very similar chocolate bar for themselves.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，他们给当地儿童医院生病的孩子买一块巧克力，或者是给自己买一块非常类似的巧克力。

sentences.en: It doesn't need to be these momentous donations.
sentences.zh: 不需要是那种重大的捐赠。

sentences.en: You don't need to be, you know, gifting a wing at the library to feel good about giving these small acts of generosity seem to be enough to lead us to feel good about giving.
sentences.zh: 你不需要，你知道的，给图书馆捐赠一栋楼来对给予感到高兴，这些小小的慷慨行为似乎就足以让我们对给予感到高兴。

sentences.en: And part of the reason I think for that is that we're just extremely social creatures.
sentences.zh: 我认为其中的部分原因在于我们是非常具有社会属性的生物。

sentences.en: Um, and these small acts of giving and generosity allowed us to build and facilitate and maintain these relationships we have with other people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些微小的给予和慷慨行为使我们能够建立、促进和维持我们与其他人的关系。

sentences.en: Let me ask you about another area you've been doing some research in.
sentences.zh: 让我问你关于你一直在做研究的另一个领域。

sentences.en: You published a study recently with another scientist we've had on speaking of psychology, Jillian Sandstrom, that looked at how people feel about reaching out to old friends.
sentences.zh: 你最近和我们之前在《心理学谈话》中邀请过的另一位科学家吉莉安·桑德斯特伦（Jillian Sandstrom）合作发表了一项研究，探讨了人们对主动联系老朋友的感受。

sentences.en: What inspired that study and what did you find?
sentences.zh: 是什么启发了这项研究？你们又发现了什么？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Jillian is, is a good friend of mine and, and it was such a pleasure to work on this with her because it was a very clear example of what we joke about as me search, not research,
sentences.zh: 吉莉安是我的好朋友，能和她一起做这个研究非常荣幸，因为这是一个非常典型的例子，也就是我们开玩笑说的“自我研究”（me search），而不是研究（research），

sentences.en: me search, um, because Jill and I have been friends since we were graduate school buddies and, um, we kind of, she moved to the UK.
sentences.zh: “自我研究”，因为我和吉尔从研究生院时期就是好伙伴，然后，嗯，她搬到了英国。

sentences.en: I stayed in Canada.
sentences.zh: 我留在了加拿大。

sentences.en: And although we've had projects to keep us connected over the years, those kind of wax and wane.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们多年来一直有项目来保持联系，但那些项目总是时断时续。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, because I'm not good at keeping in touch when projects end, I don't get to speak to her as regularly.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，因为我不擅长在项目结束后保持联系，所以我不能经常和她讲话。

sentences.en: Um, and about two years ago on
sentences.zh: 嗯，大约两年前的

sentences.en: New Year's day or around New Year's, I realized that I hadn't spoken to her.
sentences.zh: 元旦那天或元旦前后，我意识到我一直没跟她说话。

sentences.en: I really missed her.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想念她。

sentences.en: Um, and so I sent a text message saying, I miss you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我发了一条短信说，我想你了。

sentences.en: We should find a new project to work on so we can connect.
sentences.zh: 我们应该找个新项目来做，这样我们就能联系上了。

sentences.en: Um, and originally the project was designed to look at what kind of situations encourage people to reach out to old friends.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最初这个项目旨在研究什么样的情境会鼓励人们主动联系老朋友。

sentences.en: Like I had taken New Year's as an opportunity, this inspiration, this excuse, if you will, to reach out to Jillian.
sentences.zh: 就像我曾把新年当作一个机会、一种灵感、可以说是一个借口去联系吉莉安一样。

sentences.en: Um, but we, you know, as we started exploring this question, we just found that no matter what kind of situations
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是我们，你知道，随着我们开始探索这个问题，我们发现无论我们向人们抛出什么样的情况

sentences.en: we threw at people as excuses to reach out to old friends, uh, they were particularly reluctant to do so.
sentences.zh: 作为联系老朋友的借口，呃，他们都特别不愿意这样做。

sentences.en: And so, uh, we've spent the last two years trying to explore whether people have old friends, you know, the people that they care about, but they've lost touch with.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，在过去的两年里，我们一直在努力探索人们是否有老朋友，你知道，那些他们关切却失去联系的人。

sentences.en: And the answer seems to be yes.
sentences.zh: 而答案似乎是肯定的。

sentences.en: What excuses people think are valid to reach out to old friends.
sentences.zh: 人们认为什么样的借口联系老朋友才算合理。

sentences.en: The short story is not many.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，没几个。

sentences.en: The only one that seems that people will endorse is reaching out for a birthday.
sentences.zh: 唯一一个人们似乎认可的借口就是为了生日而联系。

sentences.en: Um, and then we tried to find ways we, well, we tried to benchmark this reluctance.
sentences.zh: 嗯，接着我们试图寻找方法，我们，好吧，我们试图用基准来衡量这种不情愿的心理。

sentences.en: We found that people are as willing to reach out to an old friend as they are to pick up garbage, um, and talk to a complete stranger.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，人们主动联系老朋友的意愿，和他们去捡垃圾、跟完全陌生的路人说话的意愿差不多。

sentences.en: And then we tried to figure out ways to get people to do it.
sentences.zh: 然后我们试图找出让人们行动起来的方法。

sentences.en: And that wasn't easy.
sentences.zh: 这可不容易。

sentences.en: We found one way.
sentences.zh: 我们找到了一个方法。

sentences.en: Um, but we hit, we hit a lot of roadblocks before we found one successful intervention.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是在找到一个成功的干预措施之前，我们遇到了很多阻碍。

sentences.en: And what is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么呢？

sentences.en: The successful intervention is getting people to basically do a warmup or practice activity.
sentences.zh: 成功的干预措施就是让人们基本上做热身或练习活动。

sentences.en: So in one experiment, we recruited about 200 people on a university campus.
sentences.zh: 所以在其中一个实验中，我们在大学校园里招募了大约200人。

sentences.en: All of these individuals told us that they had an old friend that would, that is someone they care about, but they've lost touch with.
sentences.zh: 所有这些人告诉我们，他们都有一个老朋友，也就是说，他们关心这个人，但已经失去了联系。

sentences.en: This is also someone who they think would be happy to hear from them.
sentences.zh: 这也是一个他们认为听到自己消息会很高兴的人。

sentences.en: And they have contact information for, um, and then one group was randomly assigned to this warmup practice task where they sent a couple messages to current friends and family.
sentences.zh: 而且他们有联系方式，嗯，然后其中一组被随机分配到这个热身练习任务中，他们向现在的朋辈和家人发送了几条消息。

sentences.en: The other half was randomly assigned to simply browse Facebook.
sentences.zh: 另一半人被随机分配到仅仅浏览Facebook的任务中。

sentences.en: So kind of, or any social media they choose.
sentences.zh: 所以有点像，或者他们选择的任何社交媒体。

sentences.en: So it was kind of a passive social comparison.
sentences.zh: 所以这算是一种被动的社会比较。

sentences.en: And then when three minutes were up, um, we asked people to draft a message to an old friend and we gave them the opportunity to send it.
sentences.zh: 然后在三分钟结束后，嗯，我们请人们起草一条给老朋友的信息，并且我们给了他们发送的机会。

sentences.en: And what we found was in our control condition, very similar to our previous experiments, only about 30% of people
sentences.zh: 我们发现，在我们的对照组中，和之前的实验非常相似，只有大约30%的人

sentences.en: were willing to hit send to send that message they had just drafted.
sentences.zh: 愿意点击发送他们刚刚起草的那条信息。

sentences.en: But in the experimental condition where people had practiced for three minutes prior, um, it was almost double that.
sentences.zh: 但在实验组中，人们在此之前已经练习了三分钟，嗯，这个比例几乎翻了一倍。

sentences.en: It was just over 50%.
sentences.zh: 刚刚超过50%。

sentences.en: What are you working on now?
sentences.zh: 你现在在做什么研究？

sentences.en: What are the big questions you're trying to answer?
sentences.zh: 你试图解答的重大问题是什么？

sentences.en: Well, some of these questions are kind of emerging from this reaching out to old friends question,
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中一些问题是从这个联系老朋友的问题中衍生出来的，

sentences.en: trying to understand who are the individuals that are most likely to reach out and how people feel when they do.
sentences.zh: 试图了解最有可能主动联系的都是些什么人，以及人们在这样做时的感受。

sentences.en: Um, students in my lab are also very interested in multiple forms of generosity.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我实验室的学生对多种形式的慷慨行为也非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: So advice giving food sharing and how that makes people feel.
sentences.zh: 比如给建议、分享食物，以及这会给人们带来怎样的感受。

sentences.en: And also we have a couple of projects looking at how, um, people express their thanks to one another and what is some of the most meaningful content in a gratitude message.
sentences.zh: 此外，我们还有几个项目在研究，嗯，人们如何向彼此表达谢意，以及感恩信息中最有意义的内容是什么。

sentences.en: That all sounds interesting and uplifting, the kind of research that makes you happy to do, right?
sentences.zh: 听起来都很有趣也很振奋人心，正是那种让你做起来会感到快乐的研究，对吧？

sentences.en: Certainly.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Well, I want to thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 好的，我要感谢你今天能来参加节目。

sentences.en: This has been very interesting.
sentences.zh: 这次谈话非常有趣。

sentences.en: Thank you, Dr. Ackman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，阿克曼博士。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology 上，或者在 Apple、Spotify、YouTube 以及任何你获取播客的平台上找到《心理学对话》往期的节目。
